question: The record's question (MCI-to-AD conversion, T2, in both papers) does not exist: P-129 has no conversion analysis and detects current MCI against healthy controls. The only question for which both papers print figures is MCI against controls from resting electrophysiology (MEG in P-173, EEG in P-129; one channel under the rule). P-173 reports it only as two outcome-defined subgroup contrasts (NC vs stable MCI, NC vs progressive MCI after about 3 years), never NC vs all MCI.
metric: Recorded claim: mismatch (P-173 'AUC 0.81', which the main text does not state, against P-129 'Acc 94.76', which is its specificity). On the printed MCI-vs-control figures: accuracy with accuracy, but P-173's value is the mean accuracy of ten different classifiers, P-129's is one model's accuracy.

figures.P-173: Mean accuracy over 10 scikit-learn classifiers, 5-fold CV, Madrid MEG cohort (53 NC, 48 sMCI, 28 pMCI). sMCI vs pMCI 78% (n=76; Wilson 0.675-0.858). NC vs sMCI 79% (n=101): Wilson centre (0.79+1.9208/101)/(1+3.8416/101)=0.779, half-width 1.96*sqrt(0.79*0.21/101+3.8416/(4*101^2))/1.038=0.079 -> 0.701-0.858. NC vs pMCI 82% (n=81): Wilson 0.722-0.889. AUCs only in supplementary figures, not in the text read.
figures.P-129: MCI vs HC, Isfahan public EEG dataset (32 MCI, 29 HC), subject-wise 6x5 nested CV repeated 20 times: accuracy 90.97% +/- 0.60 (SD over repeats, not a sampling interval). Derived Wilson with n=61: centre (0.9097+1.9208/61)/(1+3.8416/61)=0.885, half-width 1.96*sqrt(0.9097*0.0903/61+3.8416/(4*61^2))/1.063=0.074 -> 0.812-0.959. AUC 0.950 +/- 0.006; specificity 94.76% (the record's 'Acc'). No conversion analysis.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists: P-129 reports no stable/progressive subgroups and no conversion result; P-173 reports no NC-vs-all-MCI contrast. On the recorded T2 question there is nothing to compare. On the only shared question (MCI vs controls): NC vs sMCI 79% [0.701-0.858] against 90.97% [0.812-0.959] - each estimate lies outside the other's interval; NC vs pMCI 82% [0.722-0.889] - 0.9097 lies outside P-173's interval, 0.82 lies just inside P-129's (one-way only).
performance_validity: Passes: P-129 cross-subject nested-CV accuracy 0.9097 and AUC 0.950 are below 0.97 (its intra-subject 0.979/0.987 on 27/34-subject subsets are not the figures compared); P-173's accuracies are 0.61-0.82.

candidate_explanations.difference: Classifier averaging: P-173's figure is the mean of ten off-the-shelf classifiers (including decision tree, naive Bayes, QDA), not a tuned model; P-129 reports a purpose-built transformer.
candidate_explanations.quote: To assess performance irrespective of a particular classifier, we averaged the classification accuracy of ten popular classifiers

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition / population subset: P-173's MCI arms are defined by outcome after about 3 years of follow-up; P-129's MCI group is unselected by course.
candidate_explanations.quote: the stable MCI group (sMCI, n = 48) comprising those patients that still fulfilled the diagnosis criteria of MCI at the end of follow-up, and the progressive MCI group (pMCI, n = 28)

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort and recording: Madrid memory-clinic 'MCI due to AD' with MEG versus an Isfahan cardiac-catheterization-unit EEG dataset.
candidate_explanations.quote: subjects admitted to the cardiac catheterization units at Sina and Nour Hospitals in Isfahan, Iran [28]. The dataset comprised 32 subjects diagnosed with MCI and 29 healthy controls

candidate_explanations.difference: Features and input: alpha-band MEG mutual-information networks embedded by MG2G versus raw multichannel EEG into a spatio-temporal transformer; validation 5-fold CV versus repeated nested CV.
candidate_explanations.quote: All metrics were averaged over the 20 nested CVs, reported as mean ± standard deviation.

reason: The recorded disagreement is a misreading: P-129 has no conversion result and its 94.76% is specificity, so conditions 1 and 6 fail for the pair as recorded. The papers do print MCI-against-control accuracies (P-173 NC/sMCI 79%, NC/pMCI 82%; P-129 90.97%), and by the rule's interval arithmetic these differ beyond uncertainty with no matched figure, but only if outcome-defined subgroup contrasts reported as a ten-classifier mean are accepted as the same comparison as unselected MCI vs controls. That interpretive step is why the pair is borderline rather than a clear yes or no; the candidate explanations are not shown to be sufficient by either paper.
